I don't think "everyone you know disagrees" is a reason to change my mind. That's social pressure, not an argument. The people around you likely share similar backgrounds and incentives — plenty of researchers, including Haidt, Twenge, and others, have documented pretty serious harms. I'd rather be the only one in the room and still be honest than flip because the consensus in your circle leans the other way.

If you've got actual reasons — specific benefits that outweigh the anxiety, polarization, and attention damage — I'm genuinely willing to hear them. But I'm not going to abandon a view I think is true just because it's unpopular in your conversations.
